summary: A sound statement of direction but far from implementable as written: its biggest gap is that candidates and acceptance are owned by Kyyn yet never defined (unit of change, what is validated, atomicity, and which writes need them).

questions.text: What is a candidate (its unit of change), what does acceptance validate, and is acceptance atomic across several changes?
questions.reason: Decides the staging store, validation scope and rollback; the ADR only lists 'candidates, acceptance' among what Kyyn owns.

questions.text: Which writes must go through candidate/acceptance and which ordinary actions apply directly?
questions.reason: Sets the gated vs direct write paths; the ADR only says v1 wrapped 'too many ordinary actions in governance' and rejects a governance engine.

questions.text: In what form does a KB express its types, validation, calculations, tools and views, and how does Kyyn load and execute them?
questions.reason: Determines the whole loader/executor design; the ADR rejects a standalone-code requirement and lets KBs depend on Kyyn, but picks no format.

questions.text: Are unknown and disputed values a kernel-level state on every field, or modelled by each KB in its own types, and what shape does a disputed value take?
questions.reason: Affects persisted shapes, validation, calculations and views across all KBs; the ADR only requires that such values be preserved.

questions.text: What is the persistence substrate and on-disk layout of a KB and its candidates?
questions.reason: Decides history, diff, candidate isolation and atomic accept; the ADR says 'local-first' and that the runtime removes persistence work, nothing more.

questions.text: Through which interface(s) do external agents and schedulers call ordinary Kyyn operations, and is one canonical?
questions.reason: Shapes packaging, process lifetime and whether KB tools are exposed dynamically; the ADR only says external callers invoke 'ordinary Kyyn operations'.

questions.text: Must KB tools declare their effects, and does Kyyn enforce, preview or only report them?
questions.reason: Decides the tool-execution protocol; the ADR wants 'explicit effects and visible consequences' but only rules out hostile-code containment.

questions.text: Who may accept a candidate: only the human, or also the agent or a scheduler under policy?
questions.reason: Decides whether accept is an ordinary harness operation and the audit trail; the ADR says the human must be able to inspect and challenge, not who accepts.

questions.text: Is sharing or sync of a KB between machines or people in scope?
questions.reason: Multi-writer use needs conflict handling and concurrency control for candidates; 'local-first' implies a local source of truth but does not exclude sync.

questions.text: How does a KB declare the Kyyn version or API it depends on, and what happens on a mismatch?
questions.reason: Sets the compatibility guarantee and loader refusal/migration path; the ADR only says 'KBs may depend on Kyyn to execute'.

questions.text: Does one runtime discover and serve several KBs at once, and can KBs refer to each other?
questions.reason: Decides KB-scoped routing, registry/config and per-KB failure handling; the ADR names 'discovery' without saying of what.

questions.text: Are KB calculation results stored as facts or recomputed on read?
questions.reason: Stored results need invalidation and must join acceptance and validation; the ADR only says the KB owns calculations.

questions.text: What do KB-owned views render to, and does Kyyn host the surface they render into?
questions.reason: Decides whether Kyyn ships a web server/UI shell or only structured output; the ADR says 'workbench' and that the KB owns views.

questions.text: What does it mean in practice for the human to challenge a fact's meaning?
questions.reason: A challenge could be a comment, a disputed state, a revert or a new candidate, each with different data; the ADR requires the ability but not its form.

questions.text: What form do KB instructions take and how does Kyyn deliver them to the agent?
questions.reason: Decides whether instructions are passive files, a served resource or tool/kind metadata; the ADR only lists instructions among KB-owned things.
